- If sentiment is negative (e.g., -0.50) in recent days, reduce forecast peak and avoid over-optimistic trends.  
- If sentiment is positive (e.g., 0.50) and forecast is rising, check for overshoot — cap upward momentum after 2–3 consecutive days of high sentiment.  
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >5% from prior day), model tends to overcorrect — reduce forecast slope for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.00/0.20), model often overestimates — apply a 3–5% downward bias to forecast mean.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., after 50+ point spike, price drops sharply), model tends to lag — adjust forecast to reflect earlier correction.  
- For 30-day horizon, if model is consistently forecasting 1–2% above true outcome, apply a 1–2% downward adjustment to avoid overconfidence bias.
